public.prompt: A React Server Component reads product data with a server-only client, then passes an ordinary inline `onBuy` function to a `'use client'` purchase button. The framework rejects that prop at the boundary. Buying only needs serializable product data and browser-side interaction code. Which refactor preserves the split?

options.label: Mark the data-reading parent `'use client'` so the inline function no longer crosses a server boundary.
Pass serializable product fields, and create the click handler inside the client purchase component.
Convert the inline function to source text, then reconstruct and invoke it inside the client component.

answerProof.summary: The Server Component can retain server-only data access and pass supported data values across the client boundary; the Client Component then owns its browser event handler without serializing an ordinary function.
decisiveConstraints: Server-only catalog access must stay outside the client module graph.
Props crossing into the Client Component must be serializable.
The interaction implementation can live entirely on the client side.

claims.statement: Props passed from a Server Component to a Client Component must use React-supported serializable values.
Ordinary functions are not supported serializable props across that boundary, while client event handlers can be defined within the client module subtree.

optionRationales.explanation: Moving the parent into the client module graph also moves its dependencies toward client evaluation, conflicting with the server-only catalog access.
optionRationales.plausibility: Functions can be passed normally between components that are already inside the same client module subtree.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: The parent must continue executing its catalog read on the server.

optionRationales.explanation: Only data crosses the boundary, and the Client Component creates the function where event handling actually executes.
Function source is not the function's closed-over server environment, and evaluating text in the browser creates an unsafe, incomplete substitute.
optionRationales.plausibility: Strings are serializable values and can technically carry JavaScript-looking text across a boundary.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: The original function closes over server values and is not a supported client prop.
